title: Invocation microburst meter and channel-aware alert adapter
author: Aisha Kapoor
commits:
add microburst meter for per-invocation burst detection
- records short-window qps/token bursts
- exposes histogram + burst_count metric

introduce channel-aware alert adapter
- maps microburst signal to channel-specific thresholds
- integrates with existing alert router
- feature flag: obs.microburst.channel_adapter

dashboard and docs
- add microburst overview dashboard with token-latency correlation panel
- document tuning guide and rollout steps

fix tests and flake issues
- stabilize synthetic workload in test harness
- small perf improvements to meter aggregation
description:
Context and motivation: We currently see high tail latency and cost spikes originating from short-lived invocation bursts in a subset of customer channels (webhooks vs SDK). Existing SLO alerting emits global alerts that either over-notify on noisy channels or under-react to concentrated microbursts. This PR adds a lightweight per-invocation microburst meter plus a channel-aware alert adapter to reduce noise and improve signal fidelity.

What this change does (summary):
- Introduces telemetry/metrics/microburst_meter.go: a streaming aggregator that maintains exponentially decayed windows (250ms, 1s, 5s) per invocation key and emits: microburst_count, microburst_rate, microburst_token_histogram. The meter is quantile-friendly and optimized for low-allocation hot paths.
- Adds channel-aware alert adapter (alerts/rules/channel-aware-slo.yaml + runtime glue): maps configured channel profiles to dynamic thresholds derived from baseline percentiles and recent microburst_rate. Adapter supports per-channel suppressions and severity remapping.
- Dashboard: observability/dashboards/microburst-overview.json contains a consolidated view: per-channel burst heatmap, token-latency cross-correlation, kernel-queueing vs burst_count panel and a synthetic-replay sparklines widget.
- Docs: docs/observability/microburst.md describes metrics, tuning knobs, recommended thresholds for common workloads and rollback steps.
- SDK helper: small convenience in sdk/python/redwood/telemetry.py to tag invocations with channel identifiers for better attribution.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests: microburst_test.go covers aggregation semantics and boundary conditions.
- Integration: CI runs the synthetic-replay harness to validate end-to-end emission and alert adapter mapping.
- Canary rollout: feature gated behind obs.microburst.channel_adapter; staged rollout to 5% of hosted traffic then 25% with observability dashboards monitored for false positives and missed incidents.
- Fallback: adapter supports automatic quiet-window fallback to global thresholds if channel baselines are insufficient (safe default).

Key implementation notes and tradeoffs:
- Chose short decay windows (250ms, 1s, 5s) to emphasize microbursts that correlate with token-level latency spikes. This trades higher cardinality for better short-tailed detection; adapter aggregates by channel to keep cardinality bounded.
- Microburst histograms use fixed bucketing to keep ingestion costs predictable. We intentionally avoid high-cardinality labels on the histogram itself.
- The adapter applies percentile-based scaling (e.g., threshold = baseline_p95 * scaling_factor) so ops can tune sensitivity without touching metric collectors.

Files changed (high-level):
- telemetry/metrics/microburst_meter.go: core aggregation and export hooks
- telemetry/metrics/microburst_test.go: unit tests and synthetic workload harness
- telemetry/collection/pipeline.yml: wire up new metrics to graphite/ingest pipeline with sampling tiers
- alerts/rules/channel-aware-slo.yaml: new rule templates and example channel profiles
- observability/dashboards/microburst-overview.json: dashboard panels and links to runbook
- docs/observability/microburst.md: operator-facing guide and tuning playbook
- sdk/python/redwood/telemetry.py: tag helpers and example usage
- scripts/release/telemetry_migration.sql: lightweight migration to populate baseline percentiles for channels (runs as part of canary)

Review notes and decisions:
- Diego: "Please ensure histogram cardinality stays bounded; prefer channel as label set and avoid including request_id-level tags." Addressed: we aggregate at channel level and only emit invocation-level counters (not per-invocation histograms).
- Harper: "How will this interact with the existing warmup/prefix caching metrics?" Response: meter ignores prefix-warmup periods via a short warmup flag to avoid warmup transients; documented in microburst.md.
- Evan: "Can we add a quick experiment to prove reduction in alert volume?" Added an A/B replay in the synthetic harness and included baseline numbers in the PR body comments.

CI and validation:
- CI summary: build / unit tests / integration (synthetic replay) / lint all passed on run #312 (flaky replay rerun resolved).
- Performance: microburst meter adds ~1.2% CPU to the telemetry worker under a 1k-rps synthetic load in local profiling; memory overhead is bounded and documented.

Release notes:
- Add new microburst_* metrics and a channel-aware alert adapter to reduce noisy SLO alerts and detect concentrated short-lived invocation bursts. Includes dashboard and tuning guide.

Backwards compatibility and migration:
- No breaking changes to existing metrics; the new metrics are additive. The migration script seeds initial channel baselines; adapter will fall back to safe defaults if migration not run.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Add automatic threshold autotuning (deferred) once we have 30d of channel baselines.
- Extend meter to optionally export pre-aggregated microburst fingerprints for downstream anomaly detection.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals.

Conversation (highlights):
- Diego Alvarez (reviewer): "Approach looks good. Please add a safety net to avoid alert storms during migration."
- Aisha Kapoor (author): "Added quiet-window fallback and explicit migration step; documented rollback. PTAL."
- Harper Nguyen (reviewer): "Dashboard panels are useful; can you add a panel comparing channel p95 before/after adapter?"
- Aisha Kapoor: "Added pre/post replay comparison to the dashboard JSON and included sample data."
- Evan Brooks (approver): "LGTM after CI green and small test flake fixed."

Notes for oncall and SRE:
- If alerts spike after rollout, toggle obs.microburst.channel_adapter off via feature flag and run telemetry/scripts/replay_ab_test.sh to reproduce. The release includes an automated alert that fires only to the rollout channel for the first 24 hours.

Related work: ENG-2410 (observability tuning epic), ENG-2411 (dashboard refresh), several prior EX and telemetry PRs influenced metric names and conventions.

Signed-off-by: Aisha Kapoor, Observability team
